lyrics:
[Intro: bouncing synth organ riff, four-on-the-floor kick, oohs]
(Ooh, ooh-ooh)
Where do we go?

[Chorus: soulful male lead, female voices answer]
Where do we go when the lights come on?
(Tell me, tell me)
Where do we go when the song is gone?
(Not yet, not yet)

[Verse 1: male lead, beat thins to bass and hi-hat]
The floor is full and I am counting hours
The mirror ball is running out of stars
I've held this feeling like a glass of water
Don't make me spill it in the dark

[Chorus: full beat, synth riff, female voices answer]
Where do we go when the lights come on?
(Tell me, tell me)
Where do we go when the song is gone?
(Not yet, not yet)

[Verse 2: male lead, strings pad underneath]
Somebody's sweeping round the edges
Somebody's stacking up the chairs
If this is all, then say it's all
If there is more, then tell me where

[Chorus: full beat, synth riff, female voices answer]
Where do we go when the lights come on?
(Tell me, tell me)
Where do we go when the song is gone?
(Not yet, not yet)

[Breakdown: kick drops out, piano chords and voices]
(Ooh, ooh-ooh)
One more
(Ooh, ooh-ooh)
Just one more

[Build: snare roll, riff filters back in]
Where do we go?
Where do we go?
Where do we go?

[Final Chorus: everything, ad-libs, extra percussion]
Where do we go when the lights come on?
(Tell me, tell me)
Where do we go when the song is gone?
(Not yet, not yet)
Where do we go when the lights come on?
(Tell me, tell me)
Where do we go?

[Outro: riff alone, kick stops, room noise]
(Not yet)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 124 BPM, 4/4, G minor. A bright, bouncing club pulse under a minor-key melody. Dance-floor melancholy.

VOICE: Male baritone with a warm, soulful, slightly smoky tone and real gospel weight on the long notes. He sings the question as if he means it. Two female voices sing wordless 'ooh' lines and the short bracketed answers, airy and high.

INSTRUMENTS: A bouncing, percussive synth organ riff that doubles as the bass line. A hard four-on-the-floor kick with off-beat open hi-hats and a clap. A string-synth pad. House piano chords in the breakdown. A snare roll and filter sweep for the build. Shaker and tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the riff, the kick and the female oohs, with the question sung once. 0:16 Chorus 1. 0:32 Verse 1, the beat thins. 0:47 Chorus 2. 1:03 Verse 2. 1:18 Chorus 3. 1:34 Instrumental, the riff with a counter-melody. 1:49 Breakdown, the kick drops out for piano and voices. 2:20 Build, the question repeated over a snare roll. 2:36 Final chorus, twice through, with ad-libs. 3:22 Outro, the riff alone, the kick stops, a little room noise and one last answer at 3:40.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-90s Eurodance: punchy, bright and uncomplicated, kick and riff at the front, vocal with a short bright reverb.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The synth riff with the kick in the first two bars. It is built so that heads start nodding before anyone decides to.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The singer is at the end of the night and knows it, which reads as a much bigger subject to anyone old enough to remember the original. The room noise at the end is the lights actually coming on.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Elation with a shadow, bargaining for one more song, then acceptance.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

The night is nearly over, the staff are stacking chairs, and someone on the dance floor asks the only question that matters.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: closing time; the end of a relationship's good years; the end of youth; or the largest version of the question, about what follows a life. The beat never stops to answer.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an unanswerable question as the hook, a sad soulful voice over a bright dance beat, a wordless female line, and a riff built for nodding along. Designed mishearing: 'when the lights come on' is heard as 'when the life's gone wrong'.
